precepts.text: A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; Saul had two chances to repent and confess and still justified himself, so Samuel did exactly what the scripture says and rejected him.
precepts.point: Samuel refuses: I will not return with thee; for thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord hath rejected thee from being king over Israel. Think it through: Samuel gave Saul the opening at the bleating of the sheep, and Saul would not humble down; he asked why Saul disobeyed the voice of the Lord, and Saul justified himself again. Two admonitions were given and refused before this rejection.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
“I will not return with thee: for thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord hath rejected thee from being king over Israel.” Think it through. Samuel gave Saul the opening at the bleating of the sheep, and Saul would not humble down; he asked why Saul disobeyed the voice of the Lord, and Saul justified himself again. Two admonitions were given and refused before this rejection.

“A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject”. Saul had two chances to repent and confess and still justified himself, so Samuel did exactly what the scripture says and rejected him.

precepts.point: They are reprobate. It is impossible to repent after that.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
“A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject.” Once they go to heresy and do not want to repent, after the first and second admonition the heretic is rejected. The Most High will take away their spirit.

They are reprobate, and it is impossible to repent after that. So Paul says of whoever preaches another gospel, “let him be accursed”: there is nothing left to do with a heretic but reject him.

Some of us do not think we can overcome anything, but you can overcome anything, as long as you are living in these commandments. Some people see our shortcomings, but they have not seen our perfection yet; they are going to.

“This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly”. We have to affirm it constantly, “that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works.” Satan is at work, and our mind is against us, so we have to constantly maintain the good works and take full control.

That is why we have to constantly ask each other: brother, did you read your four chapters today? Sister, did you watch the captain's class, the bishop's class, anything today? If you are not watching these things, you are entertaining something else; remember how fast the thoughts are. And when the Bible is not open between a brother and a sister talking in a corner for an hour or two, it is always going to be gossip.

Satan attacked Job through his children and his wealth, and Job's wife said, Curse God and die, and Job checked her: all this time we lived a good life and never heard curse God; good comes with evil, and you speak like a foolish woman. Because she was checked, the Lord was able to bless Job at the end with new children and new wealth. Not every wealth is good.

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

precepts.why:
Not by our righteousness: “For I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.” He gave Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba for us, “Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.”

“Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up”, “bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth; Even every one that is called by my name: for I have created him for my glory, I have formed him; yea, I have made him.” He is going to do all this for us. Even though we are wicked and evil, look at our people out there, he is still going to do it for us. When he died, he died for us.

“And let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.” We all have to learn to maintain good works. When you become an officer or a captain, maintain good works; don’t stop doing what you’re doing.

We wish to see how you conduct yourself when you’re demoted. Brothers who pull back from helping the rest of the body because they lost their rank show they were only in it for a position. Nobody ever says, I’m not going to do anything until I get my rank back, but we can tell by your actions where your heart is: you want a flattering title, and you don’t really have love for the people.

On the other side, if you desire to be moved up, operate a rank above where you are. If you’re a soldier, operate as an officer of 10; an officer of 10, as an officer of 20; an officer of 20, as an officer of 50; a 50, as a captain. We want to see how you can move the people. That is what we look for.

points: Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work. Now some of you might not like that verse. It is telling you, like Romans 13, obey the powers that be — obey the laws of the land. If we do not bring stuff like that out, you will be like that young boy we saw cursing out the cops after he stole the brandy, and then you get knocked upside the head. And now your parents want to know why your child was acting up.

We never say all police are good — some of them are no damn good. But you have got to teach your kids to obey the powers that be and keep the laws of the land, as long as they do not contradict God's laws.

points: To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men. When it says speak evil of no man, that is talking about gossip.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain. Brothers, when we are teaching, we're not there to convince anybody of anything, and we're not there to argue. Arguing will not win a soul; debating will not win a soul. We are there to teach. Whether they accept it or not is up to Messiah. We are there to plant that seed.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

points: A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject. Don't argue back and forth: reject. Once you put the law down and they don't want to hear it, that's it; you got to go. Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

points: For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures: bitterness is one of those lusts. Living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another: when you have the root of bitterness you are literally living in malice. Do not be a hater; stop the hate. We learned that spirit here in this captivity.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: We ourselves, Paul says, and this goes for us: we ourselves were also sometimes foolish, disobedient to God's laws, deceived. At one time in our life we believed that Jesus was white, God was white. We thought that foolishness.
We also served divers lusts in the clubs, celebrating Christmas, Kwanzaa, Thanksgiving; and we gave in to pleasures, committing adultery.
We lived in malice, we hated each other, and envy, we were jealous of one another. Our people as a whole are hateful and hating one another.

That's the problem with the black and Latino community: we hate one another. That's why there's such a thing called black-on-black crime. You never hear about Chinese-on-Chinese crime, you don't hear about white man on white man crime. It has reached a zenith where we hate one another and we kill one another.
Listen to what Paul was telling Titus to do: be subject to principalities, governments, and powers, and obey magistrates. The Lord wants us to obey magistrates.
Pay your taxes. Get legally married. Get paperwork, a covenant, like it says in the book of Tobit.
A lot of us don't like to pay taxes. The scripture says we have got to be subject to magistrates.
We can't just throw our children away. No. We have to use wisdom when dealing with this. We have to obey the laws of the land when dealing with our children.
Put them in mind to be subject to principalities: you have to be subject to the laws of the land, to the government, to the local laws.

To obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work: you have to obey magistrates and be ready for every good work. So those younger children, you have to keep the laws of the land with them. You have to raise them to the best of your ability till they get of age and then they can make their decision. They become 18, whatnot. They don't want to keep the commandments of God, then bam, you got a decision to make. You can let them go live with a family member or help them out. Whatever you need to do. But you never know, that child can repent one day.

We have to move like the scriptures say, maintaining the best relationship we have. If they underage, you have to obey the laws of the land with them. If the children's underage and decide to go live with an unbelieving parent or whatnot, you might have to support that child, and you need to do that. You have to support that child till they become of age. And then when they become of age, they can make their decision whether they're going to keep the commandments or not.

“Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers”: we can’t speak evil of any man or be brawlers. “But gentle”: be humble, “shewing all meekness unto all men”, righteous toward all men.

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

points: “For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures”: we were foolish once, partying, having a good time, “living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.”

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

points: “But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared”: after all that, after we changed, after we repented. “Not by works of righteousness which we have done”: nothing we did. We are not such righteous brothers that he said, I’m going to gather them because they are so perfect and holy. Not for our righteousness: “but according to his mercy he saved us.”
